brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS - For TechIQ Attendees

questions.question: How many modules make up the CTFS platform?
choices: Three modules
Four modules
Five modules
Six modules
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—GrantPlan, Connect, Contracting, Forecasting, and Site Payments are the five modules that form the unified financial backbone.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Take another look at Slide 12. The five modules are GrantPlan, Connect, Contracting, Forecasting, and Site Payments—each one handles a distinct part of the financial lifecycle.

questions.question: What is Gilbert's primary frustration as a Clinical Operations Director?
choices: Integration complexity and compliance risk
Manual financial drag and fragmented visibility across studies and sites
Cash flow unpredictability and chasing multiple sponsors
Lack of AI orchestration across clinical operations
questions.feedback_correct: You've got it—Gilbert's world is trial execution, and his pain centers on manual processes, lack of visibility, and slow reconciliation that frustrates sites.
questions.feedback_incorrect: That's a pain point for a different persona. Gilbert, the Clinical Operations Director, is focused on trial execution and the operational friction caused by manual financial drag and fragmented visibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four buyer personas you will meet at TechIQ?
choices: Rachel, Site Operations Director
Andres, Digital Transformation Leader
Marcus, Finance Operations Manager
Reena, VP IT Clinical
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the four personas are Gilbert, Rachel, Reena, and Andres. Marcus is not one of the core personas covered in this course.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Review Slides 6-9. The four personas are Gilbert (Clinical Operations Director), Rachel (Site Operations Director), Reena (VP IT Clinical), and Andres (Digital Transformation Leader).

questions.question: What does CTFS Contracting NOT do?
choices: Streamlines authoring and amending clinical trial agreements
Uses agentic AI to extract and contextualize contract terms
Automatically connects payment milestones to signed contract terms
Replaces the need for any human legal review of contracts
questions.feedback_correct: Right—while Contracting uses intelligent AI to extract and contextualize terms, it streamlines the process rather than eliminating the need for human oversight entirely.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Contracting is a powerful tool that uses agentic AI to process CTAs, but it is designed to streamline and support the process, not eliminate human judgment and legal review.

questions.question: How much annual savings is CTFS Contracting projected to deliver for high-volume sponsors?
choices: Approximately $500,000 per year
Approximately $1.5 million per year
Approximately $3 million per year
Approximately $10 million per year
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the projection is $3 million in annual savings for high-volume sponsors running 100+ trials per year, assuming two CTAs per site and 200 sites per trial.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Check Slide 21. The business case shows a projected $3 million in annual savings for high-volume sponsors, based on the cumulative cost of manual CTA ingestion at scale.

questions.question: What is the key distinction about CTFS Contracting that separates it from a standalone contract tool?
choices: It uses basic OCR scanning instead of intelligent AI models
It stores contracts in a centralized database for easy access
When a CTA is signed, payment milestones and budget alignment automatically update across the platform
It requires manual data entry between Contracting and other modules
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—Slide 20 emphasizes that Contracting is not a standalone tool; signed CTAs automatically trigger payment milestones in Site Payments and update GrantPlan budgets, eliminating manual handoffs.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The power of Contracting lies in its integration. When a CTA is signed, the platform automatically connects contract terms to payment milestones and budget information—no manual transfer or reconciliation needed.

questions.question: Rachel's primary concern as a Site Operations Director is best addressed by which CTFS capability?
choices: Investigator grant benchmarking through GrantPlan
Consistent payment visibility and predictable cash flow forecasting
Integration security and compliance risk management
Agentic AI orchestration across clinical operations
questions.feedback_correct: You've connected it correctly—Rachel's pain is unpredictability and chasing multiple sponsors for payment status; CTFS delivers the consistent, unified view she needs.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look at Slide 7. Rachel's world is site-level operations and her real question is 'when will I stop chasing sponsors for payment updates?' She needs consistent visibility and forecasting.

questions.question: When delivering a pitch to a buyer who says "CTFS is new, we're not ready," what is the recommended response strategy?
choices: Argue that the technology is ready and proven in the market
Acknowledge the hesitation and pivot to proof points like $15 billion in payments processed and the sandbox pilot option
Suggest they wait until the product matures further
Emphasize that competitors are already moving, creating urgency
questions.feedback_correct: That's the right approach—acknowledge the concern first, then anchor to proven outcomes and offer a low-risk sandbox pilot so they can experience the value themselves.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Slide 25 advises against pushing back on hesitation. Instead, validate their caution and redirect to concrete proof: the $15 billion already processed and the sandbox pilot option that lets them test without risk.

questions.question: According to the course, what single characteristic is most critical when comparing CTFS to point solutions in the market?
choices: CTFS has more features than any single competitor
CTFS offers the lowest per-transaction cost
CTFS unifies the entire financial lifecycle, eliminating integration friction and data handoffs between separate systems
CTFS is the only platform with AI-driven automation
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—Slide 26 makes clear that unification is CTFS's true differentiator; while point solutions solve one problem well, they create new integration headaches that CTFS eliminates.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While CTFS has many strengths, Slide 26 emphasizes that the winning competitive story is unification. Point solutions create integration problems on both sides; CTFS solves the whole financial lifecycle without the data handoff friction.

questions.question: A prospect at TechIQ says their current system handles payments fine—what is the recommended discovery approach to open the conversation?
choices: List three reasons why their current system is inefficient
Ask what their system doesn't unify and explore the gap, which often reveals real cost
Share your CTFS feature list and show why it's superior
Acknowledge their satisfaction and move to the next prospect
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—instead of arguing, ask the gap question. The honest answer usually reveals where budgeting doesn't connect to payments or where manual reconciliation still happens, quantifying the hidden cost.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Slide 25 advises against arguing with this objection. The gap question—'what doesn't your system unify?'—almost always opens a real conversation because the answer reveals manual workarounds and disconnected processes that create cost.
